body.statement: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite family of \(s\) polynomials of maximum degree \(d\) in \(N\) real variables over an effectively represented real-algebraic coefficient field. A sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition adapted to \(\mathcal P\) can be computed, yields quantifier elimination for first-order real formulas using \(\mathcal P\), and has arithmetic complexity \((sd)^{2^{O(N)}}\).

source.locator: Section 2.1.1, the displayed Tarski--Seidenberg theorem, and Section 2.1.2, the displayed cylindrical-algebraic-decomposition theorem and the immediately following quantifier-elimination paragraph
source.verbatim_statement: For every finite set \(\mathcal P\) of polynomials in \(\mathbb R[X_1,\ldots,X_k]\), there is a cylindrical decomposition of \(\mathbb R^k\) adapted to \(\mathcal P\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the displayed CAD theorem in Saugata Basu, Algorithms in Real Algebraic Geometry: A Survey, arXiv:1409.1534; the locator also contains the stated \((sd)^{2^{O(k)}}\) bound and its quantifier-elimination consequence.
